chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas'adah ibn Sadah said: I heard Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) saying:

He was asked about a man who has a debt and owns a share in a house which yields income; sometimes its income suffices for his sustenance, and sometimes it does not, so he has to borrow. If he sells the house and pays off his debt, he is left without a house. He said: 'If in his house there is enough to pay off his debt and leave surplus sufficient for him and his dependents, let him sell the house; otherwise, let him not.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on selling a revenue-generating property to pay off debt if it is needed for family sustenance?
ai.summary: In this ruling from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of balancing debt repayment with the preservation of one's basic livelihood (*kifayah*). He clarifies that selling the property is obligatory only if the net proceeds after settling the debt still leave enough for the debtor and his family to sustain themselves; otherwise, retaining the asset to generate ongoing income is preferred to prevent destitution.
